Ravi M.: Heads-up: DSAR deletion request arrived for acct-7702. Requester notes data processed during a rolling keystore rotation window (mid-Feb). They asked for deletion proof and transcript.
Greta H.: Which keystore mode was acct-7702 on? ephemeral vs managed matters. If ephemeral and we rotated+destroyed keys, we may not be able to produce plaintext receipts for old snapshots.
Noah L.: I pulled keystore audit: acct-7702 was on ephemeral-30d. There was a scheduled rotation on 2026-02-14 and an emergency forced rewrap on 2026-02-20 due to a failed healthcheck. InfraBot: `keystore:event tenant=acct-7702 action=forced_rewrap reason=healthcheck_fail at=2026-02-20T03:42:12Z`
Ravi M.: DSAR timestamp is 2026-03-01 — within 15 days of rotation. Our erasure flow expects to read snapshot blobs and produce a signed deletion receipt. If the key material was destroyed, receipts might lack plaintext proofs.
Priya R.: Check object metadata — sometimes cold snapshots were left under old key versions and not rewrapped. If old key versions were destroyed (per ephemeral policy) we can't decrypt. But metadata (object generation, checksum, rewrap tag) can still serve as indirect evidence.
Greta H.: I queried storage: gs://redwood-embeds/snapshots/acct-7702/ shows mixed tags: ~40% rewrapped, ~60% tagged `wrapped:v2` with key-id `ephemeral-7702-v1` (that key shows `destroy_time` in KMS history).
Noah L.: If keys are destroyed, plaintext is gone. Legal will want chain-of-custody and proof we attempted retrieval and couldn't decrypt. We should start retention-exception workflow immediately.
Anya (Legal): Correct. For GDPR we must provide evidence of deletion or a documented retention exception with business justification. If plaintext cannot be reconstructed, collect and preserve all forensic artifacts (keystore audit history, OpsBot events, object manifests, job traces, KMS key lifecycle entries).
Ravi M.: Proposed immediate steps: 1) Quarantine DSAR and label as "keystore-rotation-impact" 2) Snapshot all blobs' metadata and store in an immutable audit bundle 3) Capture KMS key history and rewrap/destroy events 4) Add timeline and include run IDs of erasure jobs 5) Escalate to retention-exception board if we cannot produce full receipts
Greta H.: Also confirm RBAC changes around rotation agents. Yesterday there was an infra RBAC cleanup that removed a logging role from the rotation agent SA; if rotation ran but didn't emit structured events we may lack some logs. Check IAM change logs.
Noah L.: I found IAM audit: `policy_change actor=infra-ops removed=roles/logging.logWriter member=serviceAccount:keystore-rotator@redwood at=2026-02-19T22:10:03Z`. That aligns with the forced_rewrap event the rotator reported via OpsBot but might explain gaps in keystore logs.
Priya R.: Steps I'll take: export object manifests `gsutil ls -L`, dump KMS key history `gcloud kms keys versions list --key=projects/.../keys/ephemeral-7702 --format=json`, and collect keystore app logs and OpsBot timeline. I'll put the bundle into `gs://redwood-privacy/audit-bundles/PRV-6720/`.
Anya (Legal): Include evidence of who approved the RBAC change and why. If the RBAC change inhibited logging, document that as part of the chain. Also, prepare a templated retention-exception notice (with required approvals) in case we can't provide plaintext proofs.
Ravi M.: I'll freeze any scheduled rewraps for acct-7702 and mark the DSAR as incident PRV-6720. InfraBot: create incident PRV-6720.
InfraBot: incident PRV-6720 created, severity=medium, owner=security-oncall
Greta H.: Forensics note: even if keys destroyed, we can produce a deterministic deletion report showing: list of objects (names + generations), storage checksums, last known key-id, rotation timeline, keystore attempted access (with errors), and OpsBot rewrap event. That often satisfies legal when accompanied by an exception approval.
Noah L.: Also check whether any downstream caches (embedding KV) still hold decrypted text; those are TTL-bound and might have been scrubbed. If any caches still hold data, we must re-run erasure to purge them and produce receipts.
Priya R.: I'll scan embedding cache clusters for tenant prefix `acct-7702` and collect tombstone markers. If keys are gone, purging caches is the safe step and we can include cache purge logs in the bundle.
Anya (Legal): Once the bundle is assembled, I'll review and decide if a retention exception is necessary. If exception is approved, we must record: legal rationale, business need, and remediation plan (e.g., change ephemeral TTLs or require pre-rotation retention snapshot). If denied, we need a remediation timeline to attempt reconstruction where possible.
Ravi M.: Opening follow-ups: PRV-6721 (runbook: ephemeral pre-rotation snapshot requirement) and SEC-3010 (monitoring: missing-keystore-audit-alert). Owners: Priya (audit bundle), Greta (runbook change), Anya (legal decision). ETA: initial bundle in 24h.
Greta H.: I'll draft the runbook change: require a pre-rotation recoverability snapshot held for DSAR SLA window + copy retained under a customer-managed key when tenant opts in.
Noah L.: I'll also add a vuln-triage note: forced_rewrap due to healthcheck_fail suggests rotator could be crashing under load. Filing infra bug INFRA-8472 and linking to PRV-6720.
InfraBot: PRV-6720 updated: links=[PRV-6721,SEC-3010,INFRA-8472]
Priya R.: Bundle path: gs://redwood-privacy/audit-bundles/PRV-6720/audit-bundle.tar.gz (will upload with checksums).
Anya (Legal): After review I'll post the required wording for Support to send the requester (either deletion confirmation with artifacts or retention-exception letter). Keep all changes logged in PRV-6720.
Ravi M.: Thanks team. Keep updates in the incident. Once closed, we'll add a short post-incident runbook entry and a retro action item list.
